Being this tool useful for not only modeling your database but also for documenting it i present my takes on some usability problems and some missing functionality. I tried to keep it simple as to not overwhelm you with stuff, but this could be a great tool not only to the professional but also as a learning tool for the beginner.

These are some of the problems i encountered:

* Canvas is way too restricted, you need to make the canvas much larger in order to make a good, and usable, tool; * No panning or zooming, these are essential, and top priority in my book; * In none of the forms Enter or Return keys are mapped to the OK/Accept button, it's quite weird to tab all the way to the button (or picking up the mouse) for such a simple operation. Esc key works great in all the forms though; * Arrow on connection is on the wrong side, and no way of changing the style. I want to be able to modify the shape and style of the connection; * In the table edit form, when entering data for the fields, Enter or Return should add the field to the table, Enter on an empty definition asks the user if he wants to save the table as is; * No way of sorting the fields of a table; * No way of editing the fields once they are set; * No NULL field flag; * When creating a new table, if the name of the table is not valid, an error message appears, on closing the error the original form is gone, the user has no way to correct the error and has to start over; * Field types are scarce, and granularity is low. I understand that you are aiming for a multi database system solution, and that different databases have different types for their fields, don't try to generalize them, make the user choose the database system that he wants to develop for and present the correct types and restrictions for that specific system, perhaps present an option "Pure Modeling" option and have no restrictions and user defined types and flags, of course, this mode does not generate code; * No Field Comments; * On Canceling the table edit form, if the field definition is populated, or the fields had been changed, ask the user if he wants to ignore the changes; * On Saving the table in the edit form, if the field definition is populated, remind the user that a partial field is ready for insertion and asks if he wants to ignore it and continue;

Bugs i've found:

* **[Critical]** Given a table with a primary key that has more than one connection, if you update that table (even without changes as discussed above below) only the last connection made will be maintained, the rest will be deleted; * Click n times the help button, it opens n notes that you need to close one by one; * On Saving the table in the edit form, even if nothing changed the user is informed that the table was updated. Disable the Save Changes button, and enable it only when changes are made; * Notifications are not stacked, they are being printed on top of each other;

Sorry for the long list, i think this tool has potential and details take the most amount of time, but in my opinion they make or break a tool.

Keep the good work.

The things you are looking for confirmation on are not true. They aren't terrible, you aren't better or worse, there will be no karma hit for anyone, and her age is irrelevant. If you really need those things to be confirmed, you're coming at this from the wrong angle. That may sound harsh, and it doesn't make you a bad person to want to hear those things. But nonetheless, you aren't innocent in the way it played out.

Look, what happened here sucks, there are no two ways around it. This is a shitty way to have to learn these lessons, through first-hand exposure, but in literally the first six words of your story you identified the key problem you and this person had. "This relationship was on and off" really means "this wasn't a romantic relationship in the first place". Yeah, dude was a dick for sure (at best you may be able to call him terrible if you want), but you now know that if this is how a person acts when you want a deeper level of involvement, they don't share the same feelings.

You had an equal role in how this played out when you allowed this, " Although we were broken up, we continued to sleep with each other and hang out. It was like things hadn't changed, but I wasn't allowed to ask questions." to happen. You shouldn't do that. Ever. It's never a good thing. There is no respect for you in those sentences, from him or from yourself. He got angry when you tried to break it off because he had a good thing going and he didn't want it to end. The relationship was abusive; while not necessarily on a physical level, it was a one-way power dynamic that saw you being used. You learned the hard way not to let that happen in the future; which is something you should stay aware of if you can't identify what it is you find in yourself so unappealing that you let it happen in the first place. You seem to still have a negative self image, which could very easily allow this to happen again.

I'm not saying any of this to put you down. I'm saying it because you need to take a really hard look at what led to this happening so that it doesn't happen again because no one deserves to be treated that way. You wanted something out of him he never intended to give you and you still seem to have an image of him there is no way he could live up to. You shouldn't compare yourself with the other woman. His tastes and mate preferences are as objective as possible and in no way reflect on you as a person, but have everything to do with him. No one is ever going to be everyone's top pick. Not you, not her, not him. He didn't choose her because she was better than you, but because he felt she was more right for him. That doesn't actually mean anything about you. It's also worth noting that she did nothing wrong here. While she certainly doesn't sound like much, all she did was date a guy who she was into. The fact that she knew you really doesn't matter here; you were acquaintances, that just means it's dumb luck the two of you met at all.

What are you supposed to do? Well, what do you want to have happen from here on out? Figure it out and do that. There is no better closure for you and the longer you stay hung up on this the longer it is going to hurt. It was a bad situation, now it's not. You made mistakes, there is nothing more that you can do than gather the whole experience, throw it in the 'fail' bin, and move on. Take what you learned and apply it to your relationships going forward. Avoid viewing your self worth through the lens of another person's actions; if you only find value by being valued, you open yourself up to being taken advantage of in order to feel validated. There's nothing wrong with you. You have to realize that for yourself.
